article_title: Thousands turn out in Edinburgh to protest against AI data centres

tasks.prompt: What is the report mainly about?
options: A technology exhibition held inside the Scottish Parliament
A large Edinburgh protest over the environmental and local impact of planned AI data centres
The closure of Scotland's existing data centres
A government decision to cancel every AI project
tasks.correct_answer: A large Edinburgh protest over the environmental and local impact of planned AI data centres
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה עוסקת במחאה גדולה באדינבורו נגד מרכזי נתונים לבינה מלאכותית והשלכותיהם הסביבתיות והמקומיות.

tasks.prompt: What route did the demonstrators take?
options: From Chapelcross to Airdrie
From Larbert to Cockenzie
From the top of the Royal Mile towards the Scottish Parliament
From Edinburgh Airport to the city centre
tasks.correct_answer: From the top of the Royal Mile towards the Scottish Parliament
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המפגינים התאספו בראש ה-Royal Mile וצעדו לעבר הפרלמנט הסקוטי.

tasks.prompt: How does the planned Chapelcross site's capacity compare with Scotland's largest current data centre?
options: Both have a capacity of 12MW
Chapelcross would have 50MW rather than 1,000MW
Chapelcross would have 1,000MW, compared with about 12MW at DataVita's Airdrie site
The current Airdrie site is larger than the proposed Chapelcross site
tasks.correct_answer: Chapelcross would have 1,000MW, compared with about 12MW at DataVita's Airdrie site
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המתקן המתוכנן בצ'אפלקרוס צפוי להיות בעל הספק של 1,000MW, לעומת כ־12MW במתקן DataVita באיירדרי.

tasks.prompt: What does “moratorium” mean in the call made by the Scottish Greens and campaign groups?
options: A temporary halt to approving or building large data centres
A tax reduction for technology companies
A measurement of electricity capacity
A permanent ban on renewable energy
tasks.correct_answer: A temporary halt to approving or building large data centres
tasks.explanation_hebrew: moratorium הוא השעיה או עצירה זמנית, כאן של קידום מרכזי נתונים גדולים.

tasks.prompt: Which construction and operating concerns did Kim Cairns identify?
options: A shortage of programmers and university courses
Lower internet speeds and fewer tourists
Noise, road closures, access problems, pollution and very high electricity use
A lack of costumes and protest placards
tasks.correct_answer: Noise, road closures, access problems, pollution and very high electricity use
tasks.explanation_hebrew: קיירנס הזכירה רעש, חסימות כבישים, קשיי גישה, זיהום אוויר ואור וצריכת חשמל עצומה.

tasks.prompt: When Alyn Smith calls data centres “the whisky bonds of the AI sector”, what is he suggesting?
options: They should be used only to store whisky records
They can be major industrial assets that support economic activity
They require no planning oversight
They are small buildings with little energy demand
tasks.correct_answer: They can be major industrial assets that support economic activity
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ההשוואה למחסני הוויסקי מציגה את מרכזי הנתונים כתשתית תעשייתית חשובה שעשויה להביא תועלת כלכלית.

tasks.prompt: Why do campaigners argue that the Chapelcross proposal could have national rather than only local effects?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לקשר בין ממדי המתקן, צריכת האנרגיה וההשפעות על מדיניות ארצית.
expected_points: The proposed capacity is 1,000MW, far larger than existing Scottish facilities
Such a site would require very large amounts of electricity
Campaigners fear pressure on renewable energy supplies and higher energy bills
They argue it could affect national climate targets
The scale could create impacts beyond the immediate community

tasks.prompt: Summarise the main arguments of protesters and the Scottish government's response.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג חששות סביבתיים ומקומיים מול צעדי התכנון והטענה לתועלת ציבורית.
expected_points: Protesters fear noise, construction disruption, land use, pollution and heavy electricity demand
Campaigners say large sites could undermine climate targets and raise bills
Some groups want a moratorium and greater public control
The government says data centres may provide public benefit
New guidance is due before year-end
Applications over 50MW require notification to ministers and an Environmental Impact Assessment

tasks.prompt: Why does the government require an Environmental Impact Assessment for new data centres above 50MW?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר כיצד הסף קשור להיקף ההשפעה ולצורך בבחינה לפני אישור.
expected_points: Higher-capacity sites can use much more electricity
Large projects may affect climate goals, land, noise and local infrastructure
An assessment makes developers document likely environmental effects
The rule gives planning authorities and ministers more evidence before decisions

tasks.prompt: Write a short recommendation for how Scotland should decide whether to approve a large AI data centre.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציע תהליך מאוזן הכולל תועלת, עלויות, שיתוף ציבור ובדיקות סביבתיות.
expected_points: Measure economic and public benefits rather than assuming them
Assess electricity demand, emissions, noise, pollution and land use
Consult affected communities and consider access and construction disruption
Require a credible Environmental Impact Assessment
Consider effects on national energy supplies, bills and climate targets
